newsitem.title: USA: J. Ray McDermott sales to offset slowness.
newsitem.headline: J. Ray McDermott sales to offset slowness.

text.p: J. Ray McDermott SA said Thursday the traditional lower profitability of its second half should be partially offset by asset sales this year.

The company reported first half earnings of $0.53 per share, up from $0.21 a year earlier, on revenues of $758.3 million compared with $671.7 million for the period ended September 30. The company lost $0.46 per share in last year's second half.
It said second quarter earnings rose to $0.27 from $0.18 as revenues reached $368.7 million compared with $359.5 million a year earlier.
In North America, higher levels of fabrication and marine activity resulted in improved second quarter revenues and operating income, J. Ray McDermott said.

But North Sea revenues were significantly lower than last year's, reflecting the near-completion of the Foinaven project, leaving the area with an operating loss compared with operating income in the September 1995 quarter.

In the Middle East, revenue was about the same as last year, but the operating loss increased as improved fabrication results were offset by lower utilization of marine equipment. In the Far East, revenue and operating income increased.
Chief executive James L. Dutt said "Most of our marine construction markets remain strong, and we continued to add to our backlog during the quarter.

"In the Gulf of Mexico, Texaco (Inc ) awarded us a contract to design, fabricate, and install a compliant tower in over 1,750 feet of water." An affiliate was awarded the offshore portion of an LNG project in Qatar.
"After the close of the quarter, both Marathon (Oil Co) and Shell (Oil Co ) awarded us projects for subsea work in the North Sea.

"In total, our consolidated backlog at the end of the quarter stood at $1.5 billion compared with $835 million last year. Further, the backlog of our unconsolidated affiliates was $1.5 billion compared with $1.3 billion a year ago."

Dutt concluded, "This level of backlog strongly suggests that JRM will have improving financial results for the next several years. However, this is a seasonal business and, historically, in the second half of the fiscal year our operations have been significantly less profitable than in the first half.
"We do not expect fiscal 1997 to be an exception, but expected gains from the planned sale of surplus assets should partially offset lower second half results."
McDermott International Inc holds a majority interest in J. Ray McDermott.
